about.title: Monterey Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey's mix of coastal tourist traffic, Route 68 commuters, and local drivers on Fremont Street and Lighthouse Avenue creates plenty of opportunity for sudden collisions, especially as reported crashes tend to cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. when weekend travel picks up. In a recent year, Monterey County recorded 135 injury collisions and 171 people injured on local roads. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, what happens in the days afterward matters. Insurance adjusters move fast, sometimes asking for recorded statements before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can review your situation, explain your options, and help make sure evidence isn't lost while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that reflects your actual share of fault, not the insurer's version.

items.title: No Cap Means No Reason to Rush a Settlement
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so there's little upside to accepting an early insurance offer. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to get a second opinion.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to find reasons to reduce or deny a claim. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Route 68 or another Caltrans-maintained road?
items.answer: Claims involving state or county roadways can involve government entities, which come with much shorter notice deadlines, sometimes just six months. If your Monterey-area crash happened on a state highway or county road, it's worth having an attorney evaluate the situation quickly.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
